test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 21 Nov, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: What do you understand by 'barter system'?

options.text: purchase of goods in exchange for money
purchase and sale of goods for goods
sale of goods in exchange for money

solution:
The correct answer is __**purchase and sale of goods for goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The barter system is a method of trade where goods and services are exchanged directly for other goods and services without the use of money.
 
• This system relies on the double coincidence of wants, meaning both parties must have what the other desires.
 
• Barter systems were prevalent in ancient civilizations before the advent of money.
 
• It is still used in some communities and in situations where currency is unstable or unavailable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Double Coincidence of Wants:**

 
 
• This is a situation where two parties each possess an item the other wants, facilitating an exchange.
 
• It is a fundamental challenge in a barter system as it requires finding a matching need.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Barter:**
 
 
• Barter systems can be inefficient, especially with complex needs and large societies.
 
• The lack of a common measure of value can complicate transactions.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Bartering dates back to 6000 BC, introduced by Mesopotamian tribes and adopted by Phoenicians.
 
• Various items such as salt, spices, and weapons were commonly exchanged.
 
 
 
• **Modern Use:**
 
 
• Barter still exists in modern economies during times of monetary crisis.
 
• Some businesses use barter networks or exchanges to trade excess inventory for needed goods.
